title: security(rbac-v2): enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging hardening
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: customers operating under regional data residency and regulated environments require strict enforcement and auditability of KMS region pinning when RBAC v2 policies reference customer-managed keys. This PR tightens enforcement rules, improves audit logging semantics, and adds migration tooling for existing policies. Summary of changes: 1) Enforce KMS region pinning at policy evaluation time: policies that reference a KMS key are now checked for region residency constraints and will fail evaluation with a clear policy error if the key region does not match the resource residency policy. 2) Audit log hardening: every policy decision that touches KMS or data residency now emits a structured audit entry that includes policy id, decision, affected resource id, key arn, key_region, acting principal, request id, and evaluation trace id. Logs are written to the standard audit pipeline and include a short hash to allow cross-referencing without leaking full key material. 3) Migration tool: a safe migration that flags non-compliant policies and optionally rewrites policy bindings to include explicit kms_region pins when a matching key is available. The migration runs as an idempotent job and produces a report. 4) CLI/console UI: expose a policy validation endpoint and a preflight checker for Dedicated/Private installs so admins can detect policy violations before rollout. 5) Tests and e2e: unit tests for policy engine, integration tests against a mock KMS region registry, and e2e smoke tests exercising audit logs ingestion. 6) Documentation: doc links added to RBAC v2 policy reference and migration guide. Backwards compatibility: policy evaluation will default to audit-mode for 7 days via the feature flag "rbac_v2_kms_region_enforcement_mode": "audit" -> "enforce" transition plan. Checklist: - [x] Policy engine changes implemented - [x] Audit schema added and pipeline wired - [x] Migration job implemented with dry-run - [x] Console preflight and CLI validations added - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and release notes drafted Testing: ran unit suite, integration tests against local mock-kms, and canary on staging; CI passed on retry after a flaky tracing test. Rollout: feature gated behind "rbac_v2_kms_region_enforcement_mode" with default audit-only; Ops will flip to enforce for new customers after 7 days and for all customers after 30 days unless opted out via support ticket. Related: ENG-2145 tracking the enforcement rollout, SUP-987 support backlog item for assisted migrations. Additional notes: kept error messages stable to allow SDKs and customers to detect the special KMS_REGION_MISMATCH error code and surface guidance. This PR is non-breaking for customers while in audit mode but becomes enforcement when flag is flipped.

Sofia: Audit schema looks good but can we minimize PII? Consider removing full principal email from logs.
Author reply: We now emit principal_id and principal_type; full email is obfuscated and only available in restricted debug logs behind feature flag.
Ravi: Migration job should not auto-apply by default. Make dry-run the default and require --apply with confirmation.
Author reply: Default is dry-run; updated CLI to require --apply and interactive confirmation for interactive runs, and explicit --force for non-interactive automation.
